Summary: No manner of blood may be eaten, whether of fowl or beast, in any dwelling of Israel.
Commandment: Do not eat any manner of blood, of fowl or of beast, in any of your dwellings.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The blood was given on the altar to make atonement, not given as food. Hebrews teaches the sacrificial system pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering (Hebrews 10:1-14).
Purpose: To provide atonement, thanksgiving, and fellowship under the old covenant. Hebrews teaches these pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering (Hebrews 10:1-14), so the system ceased.
